land.text: the Syro-Hittite states of south-east Anatolia and north-west Syria, led by 'Karkemiš under Kuzi-Teššub'

successors.note: The only successor the Hittites page names. The rest of the plateau (Kaska, Phrygians, Mushki) has no dossier; by 1160 Tiglath-Pileser I was defeating the Mushki, 'much of the territory being seized by Assyria'.

capitals.name: Hattusa (Boğazkale)
capitals.note: 'sometime around 1650 BC and established his capital city at Hattusa'. In the Middle Kingdom 'the capital once again went on the move, first to Sapinuwa and then to Samuha' (no years on the page).

capitals.name: Šamuḫa (Samuha)
capitals.note: The infobox lists Šamuḫa as capital-in-exile '(1400–1350 BC)', 'In exile under Tudḫaliya III'. The coordinates are the proposed site (Kayalıpınar) and approximate.

capitals.name: Hattusa (Boğazkale)
capitals.note: Tarḫuntašša was the capital in the 'Regnal period of Muwatalli II' (infobox) with no years given, so it is not drawn. 'Hattusa was burnt to the ground sometime around 1180 BC'; the capital 'is recognized as having been abandoned around 1190 BCE'. [Reviewer me-04-a: from -1349 to -1350 and Šamuḫa to -1351, to agree with the -1350 capital_move event and the infobox 'Capital-in-exile: Šamuḫa (1400–1350 BC)'.]

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1600 shape (58,875 km2 around Hattusa and the Kızılırmak bend) taken back to the founding

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's first Hittite shape begins in -1600 but the infobox gives the establishment as c. 1650 BC and the page puts Labarna/Hattusili I's capital at Hattusa 'around 1650 BC'. The page gives no extent for the Old Kingdom's first half-century (Hattusili I 'attacked, but did not capture' Aleppo), so the -1600 shape is carried back at confidence 1.

58,875 km2 around Hattusa. Mursili I's 'great raid down the Euphrates River, bypassing Assyria and sacking Aleppo and Babylon' (1595 BC middle chronology, 1587 low) is a raid, not a conquest; the page gives no area for the Old Kingdom.

57,838 km2, the same core. The page: 'The last monarch of the Old Kingdom, Telepinu, reigned until about 1500 BC'; Kaskian attacks and capital moves mark a weak phase. Unverified at cell level: page budget; the shape is probably generous for a weak kingdom but the page offers no smaller one.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1400 shape, unchanged, but valid only for -1400..-1346

keyframe_review.note: 167,244 km2 (Cilicia, the Taurus and the Anatolian centre to 31.7 E, none of it in Syria): the Empire period 'dates from the reign of Tudhaliya I from c. 1430 BC', and Tudhaliya I 'vanquished the Hurrian states of Aleppo and Mitanni' and 'expanded to the west at the expense of Arzawa'. Years shortened: the shape holds -1400..-1346 and is replaced from -1345 by hittites_-1345 (Suppiluliuma's Syrian conquests), because Cliopatria delays them to -1300.

correction.text: the 1400 Anatolian shape plus the Hittite conquests in Syria after Suppiluliuma I's war

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'The Hittite-Syrian war is dated to 1345 BC' and Carchemish fell 'in 1327 BC' (Mitanni page); Cliopatria shows Syria only from -1300, 45 years later. The shape is the 1400 shape plus the part of the 1300 shape inside Greater Syria (Aleppo, Mukiš, Nuhašše, Kadesh, Carchemish, the coast to Ugarit and Amurru); the Anatolian west (Arzawa) is added only in -1300.

321,568 km2, the empire at its extent: the page's map caption reads 'Hittite rule c. 1300 BC'. The step from the 1400 shape adds Syria (120 cells) and 440 cells of Anatolia, mainly the west: Mursili II 'attacked Arzawa' (Mursili II page) and made treaties with Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land, so the western part was held by vassal kings (ledger). The Hittites page gives no area, so the infobox cannot be compared.
320,455 km2, 0.3 percent below 1300. Treaty of Kadesh 1258 'fixed their mutual boundaries' (Hittites page); no border moves in this decade on the pages opened.

300,838 km2, 20,000 km2 less than -1240. Tudhaliya IV (c. 1245-1215) was 'heavily defeated by Tukulti-Ninurta I of Assyria in the Battle of Nihriya'; the page gives no year or lost land, so the loss is attributed to Assyria at confidence 1.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1200 shape unchanged, valid only for -1200..-1181

keyframe_review.note: The same 300,838 km2 shape runs to -1151 but the empire ends earlier: Suppiluliuma II's reign 'began in c. 1207 BC and ended coinciding with the collapse'; the infobox ends the state c. 1200 BC and lists the last ruler as 'c. 1210–1180 BC'; 'Hattusa was burnt to the ground sometime around 1180 BC'. The shape stands for -1200..-1181 only; -1180..-1151 is no Hittite state (neo-hittite-states from -1175 in the south-east, nobody's land elsewhere).

region.text: the kingdom around Hattusa, in the bend of the Kızılırmak (Halys)

ledger.note: c. 1650 BC: Labarna I, who renamed himself Hattusili I, makes Hattusa his capital. The infobox gives the establishment as c. 1650 BC and the text has him 'sometime around 1650 BC and established his capital city at Hattusa'. The page gives the city, not a boundary; the kingdom grew out of Kussara and Kanesh (Neša), a polity c. 1750-1650.

c. 1400 BC: the court withdraws to Šamuḫa. The infobox lists it as capital-in-exile '(1400–1350 BC)', 'In exile under Tudḫaliya III'; the Middle Kingdom court had already moved to Sapinuwa (no years).

region.text: the Cilician and central-Anatolian lands added in the Empire period, with the Arzawa frontier in the west

ledger.note: c. 1400 BC: Tudhaliya I builds the first empire. 'Tudhaliya I (c. 1400 BC) vanquished the Hurrian states of Aleppo and Mitanni' and 'expanded to the west at the expense of Arzawa'; Kizzuwatna was allied with the Hittites under Telipinu and Tudhaliya I (the page's words, unquoted). Cliopatria's step adds 109,000 km2 with no Syrian cell, so the western part is Arzawa and the Cilician part (Kizzuwatna) is a bridge. Cliopatria's year; the empire period starts 'from c. 1430'.
c. 1350 BC: the court returns to Hattusa. The page ends the exile at 1350 ('(1400–1350 BC)') and does not describe the return.

region.text: Aleppo, Mukiš (Alalakh) and the other Mitanni lands west of the Euphrates

ledger.note: 1345 BC: Suppiluliuma I's Syrian war takes Mitanni's western lands. The Mitanni page dates the Hittite-Syrian war to '1345 BC' and has Washukanni sacked in it; the Suppiluliuma page names Aleppo and Mukiš as conquered 'during the One-Year War' (no year there). The Cliopatria shape shows this only from -1300.

region.text: Nuhašše, Kadesh, Qatna and the Orontes and coast kingdoms down to Amurru and Ugarit

ledger.note: c. 1345 BC (bridged): the rest of Syria falls to Suppiluliuma I. The page says Kadesh's king Šutatarra was defeated, Nuḫašši's king driven out, Qatna among 'the Syrian kingdoms he conquered after crossing the Euphrates', but gives no year; 1345 is the Mitanni page's date of the war, and his reign is 'c. 1350–1322 BC'.

region.text: Ugarit on the Syrian coast

ledger.note: c. 1345 BC (bridged): Ugarit recognises Hittite suzerainty. King Niqmaddu II recognised Suppiluliuma's suzerainty (the page's statement, no year; reign 'c. 1350–1322 BC').

region.text: Amurru, the coastal kingdom between Ugarit and Byblos

ledger.note: c. 1345 BC (bridged): Amurru passes from Egypt to the Hittites. The Suppiluliuma page says Amurru's king Aziru defied Egypt and became a Hittite vassal (no year). Ramesses II recovered it in the 1270s (see the contest below).

region.text: the Mitanni rump

ledger.note: c. 1330 BC: Shattiwaza is installed as king of what was left of Mitanni. Shattiwaza was installed by a Hittite army 'in the late 14th century BC' and 'reigned c. 1330–1305 BC' (Mitanni page); the country became 'alternately the dependency of the Hittites and the Assyrians' (Suppiluliuma page).

region.text: Carchemish on the Euphrates

ledger.note: 1327 BC: Carchemish falls. 'Carchemish too was taken after a siege' (1327 BC, during the Hittite war); the Suppiluliuma page has him install his son Piyaššili (Šarri-Kušuḫ) there as vassal king, the viceroy of Syria.

region.text: the Mitanni rump

ledger.note: c. 1305 BC (bridged): Mitanni passes to Assyrian suzerainty. Shattiwaza's reign ends c. 1305 and 'Adad-nirari claims to have captured King Shattuara and brought him to Ashur, where he took an oath as a vassal' (Mitanni page, no year).

region.text: the western Anatolian lands (Arzawa, Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla, the Seha River Land) and the northern and upper-Euphrates marches

ledger.note: c. 1300 BC (bridged): Mursili II settles the west. He turned west to resist Uhhaziti, king of Arzawa (page's words, unquoted), and the page lists treaties with Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land; the page gives no year (reign 1321-1295 on the page's short chronology). 1300 is Cliopatria's step. The 440 cells also hold Isuwa (overrun in the One-Year War, Suppiluliuma page) and the Kaska marches.

region.text: the western kingdoms held by treaty rather than rule

ledger.counterpart: Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land
ledger.note: c. 1300 BC (bridged): the Arzawa lands are Hittite vassals. The Mursili II page lists treaties with Kupanta-Kurunta (Mira-Kuwaliya), Targašnalli (Hapalla) and Manapa-Tarhunta (Seha River Land); undated.

region.text: Amurru and the Orontes valley up to Kadesh

ledger.note: c. 1275 BC (mirrored): Ramesses II retakes Amurru. The treaty page says only that the Hittites took Amurru during their Syrian campaigns (no year); the date and the loss are the Egyptian dossier's (Ramesses II in his fourth year). Page silent.

region.text: Amurru

ledger.note: c. 1275 BC (mirrored): Amurru passes back to Egypt for a year (Egyptian dossier); page silent.

region.text: Kadesh and Amurru on the Orontes and the coast

ledger.note: c. 1274 BC: Hittites and Egyptians meet at Kadesh. The treaty page puts the Battle of Kadesh around 1274 BC with neither side prevailing decisively, and says the Hittites took Amurru during their Syrian campaigns (no year); the Egyptian dossier has Ramesses II retaking Amurru c. 1275.

region.text: Amurru and Kadesh, held by the Hittites after the battle

ledger.note: May 1274 BC (mirrored): after Kadesh the Hittites hold the Orontes valley. The treaty page says the battle's outcome was not decisive; the Egyptian dossier has Egypt withdrawing to Canaan after it and the Hittites keeping Kadesh. Page silent on the land.

region.text: Amurru

ledger.note: 1274 BC (mirrored): Amurru is again a Hittite vassal (the treaty page says the Hittites took Amurru during their campaigns, no year).

region.text: Kadesh and Amurru; the border between the two empires

ledger.note: 1258 BC: Hattusili III and Ramesses II make peace. The treaty page has it ratified in the 21st year of Ramesses II's reign (1258 BC) and says it 'established boundaries for the two conflicting claims'. The Hittites page says it 'fixed their mutual boundaries in southern Canaan'; the treaty page does not name Canaan, Kadesh or Amurru. [Reviewer me-04-a: confidence 3 to 2; the treaty page names no region, the Hittites page says only 'southern Canaan', so the Homs/Tartus/North Lebanon zone is the researcher's reading.]

region.text: the 20,000 km2 by which Cliopatria shrinks the shape

ledger.note: c. 1220 BC (bridged): Assyria takes ground from Tudhaliya IV. He 'was heavily defeated by Tukulti-Ninurta I of Assyria in the Battle of Nihriya' (reign c. 1245-1215, no year); the page names no land. The Assyrian dossier should carry the matching gain.

region.text: Ugarit

ledger.note: c. 1185 BC: Ugarit is destroyed in the collapse. The page calls it a 'small seagoing vassal state (destroyed c. 1185 BC)'.

region.text: Amurru

ledger.note: c. 1180 BC: the vassalage ends with the empire.

region.text: the western kingdoms

ledger.counterpart: Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land
ledger.note: c. 1180 BC: the western vassalage ends with the empire.

region.text: the south-east: Carchemish and the Syro-Hittite states

ledger.note: c. 1180 BC: the south-east survives as the Neo-Hittite states. After Hattusa fell, 'Karkemiš under Kuzi-Teššub' expanded into a regional power; 'These Syro-Hittite states gradually fell under the control of the Neo-Assyrian Empire (911–608 BC)'.

region.text: the plateau, Cilicia and the west, left without a state

ledger.note: c. 1180 BC: the plateau is stateless. The Sea Peoples began their 'push down the Mediterranean coastline' (Cilicia and Cyprus), with Kaskian, Phrygian and Bryges invasions and 'drought for three consecutive years in 1198, 1197 and 1196 BC'; Hattusa 'burnt to the ground sometime around 1180 BC'; by 1160 'much of the territory being seized by Assyria'.

region.text: the Hittite Empire

ledger.note: c. 1180 BC: the Hittite Empire ends. Suppiluliuma II's reign 'began in c. 1207 BC and ended coinciding with the collapse of the Hittite Empire'; the infobox says disestablished c. 1200 BC, the text has Hattusa abandoned c. 1190 and burnt c. 1180. [Reviewer me-04-a: the quoted infobox 'c. 1210–1180 BC' is not on the Hittites page; replaced by the page's words.]

wars.name: Hittite raid on Aleppo and Babylon
wars.outcome: Mursili I 'conducted a great raid down the Euphrates River, bypassing Assyria and sacking Aleppo and Babylon'; no land was held and he was murdered on his return.
wars.note: 1595 BC (middle chronology) or 1587 BC; Hattusili I's earlier campaign against Yamhad 'attacked, but did not capture, its capital of Aleppo'.

wars.name: Great Syrian War (Suppiluliuma I against Mitanni)

zones.text: Aleppo, Mukiš and Mitanni's lands west of the Euphrates

wars.outcome: Hittite victory: Washukanni sacked in 1345, Carchemish taken 1327, Mitanni reduced to a Hittite dependency under Shattiwaza.
wars.note: The Suppiluliuma page names a One-Year War (Isuwa, Aleppo, Mukiš) and a Six-Year War (Carchemish, mostly fought by his deputies) without years; the Mitanni page gives 1345 and 1327.

wars.name: Mursili II's Arzawa campaign
wars.outcome: Arzawa defeated and its lands bound to the Hittites by treaties with Mira-Kuwaliya, Hapalla and the Seha River Land.
wars.note: The page gives no year for the campaign; the span is Mursili II's reign (1321-1295 on the page's short chronology).

wars.name: Hittite-Egyptian war over Kadesh and Amurru
wars.outcome: Battle of Kadesh c. 1274 BC, no decisive result; peace treaty in 1258 fixing the boundary of the two claims.
wars.note: The Egyptian dossier has the Egyptian recovery of Amurru c. 1275 and the matching contest dates.

wars.name: Hittite-Assyrian war under Tudhaliya IV (Battle of Nihriya)

zones.text: the land by which Cliopatria shrinks the Hittite shape

wars.outcome: Tudhaliya IV 'heavily defeated by Tukulti-Ninurta I of Assyria'; the shape loses 20,000 km2 between 1240 and 1220 (attribution bridged).
wars.note: No year on the page: the span is Tudhaliya IV's reign c. 1245-1215. He also 'temporarily annexed the island of Cyprus' (no year); not drawn.

wars.name: Collapse of the Hittite Empire
wars.outcome: The empire ends: Hattusa abandoned c. 1190 and burnt c. 1180; Suppiluliuma II's late naval victory against Alashiya did not stop it.
wars.note: The page lists Sea Peoples, Kaskian, Phrygian and Bryges invasions, Assyrian annexations, revolts and drought; no single cause or date.

certainty.note: Bronze Age frontiers are known from treaties and city lists, not surveyed lines; the Syrian frontier with Egypt is a treaty line only from 1258 (which the pages describe in general terms), and the western vassal lands have no boundaries at all.

notes: CLIOPATRIA ROW: one row, -1600..-1151, 7 shapes. Starts 50 years after the infobox's c. 1650 (new keyframe -1650), delays Suppiluliuma's Syria to -1300 (new keyframe -1345; the Mitanni page dates the war 1345 and Carchemish 1327), and runs 30 years past the end (Hattusa burnt c. 1180; the infobox says the empire was disestablished c. 1200, the last king c. 1210-1180); the last shape is kept to -1181 only. AREA: the Hittites page gives no area, so no comparison with Cliopatria's 321,568 km2 is possible. PAGE BUDGET: five pages (Hittites, Suppiluliuma I, Mitanni, Mursili II, Egyptian-Hittite peace treaty). The Hittites page was fetched three times for different facts; the Suppiluliuma and Mursili II pages give no years for any conquest, so the 1345-1327 dates rest on the Mitanni page and the 1300 Arzawa step on Cliopatria. NOT DRAWN, page silent on years: Tarḫuntašša as capital under Muwatalli II (no years), Sapinuwa as capital, Tudhaliya IV's temporary annexation of Cyprus (reign 1245-1215), Azzi-Hayasa vassalage after Ganuvara (Mursili II's ninth year), Kizzuwatna's incorporation (the Hittites page says only 'allied'), Isuwa (overrun in the One-Year War). A gap-filler should open 'Kizzuwatna', 'Arzawa', 'Tudhaliya IV' and 'Muwatalli II'. MIRRORS: the -1275 loss and -1274 gain (and the Amurru vassal pairs) copy the Egyptian dossier (Ramesses II retakes Amurru c. 1275, Kadesh May 1274); the treaty page is silent on both years. The Mycenaean dossier records contests with the Hittites in western Anatolia (Arzawa revolt c. 1315, Wilusa c. 1240, last Ahhiyawa record c. 1220); the Hittite pages opened give no dates for these, so they are not mirrored. COUNTERPART DOSSIERS WANTED: arzawa, kizzuwatna, ugarit, amurru, syrian-city-states (Mukiš, Nuhašše, Kadesh, Qatna), isuwa, azzi-hayasa, kaska. Gazetteer names wanted: Carchemish (a coordinate stands in), Gath, Mukiš/Alalakh, Kadesh, Amurru, Ugarit exists. DISAGREEMENT: the Hittites page says the 1258 treaty 'fixed their mutual boundaries in southern Canaan'; the treaty page says nothing of southern Canaan (the ledger follows the treaty page). The Mitanni page dates Suppiluliuma's war 1345; the Suppiluliuma page dates his reign c. 1350-1322 or 1351-1319.
